title: Design SQL
description:
# Design SQL

You are given `n` tables represented with two arrays `names` and `columns`, where `names[i]` is the name of the `i-th` table and `columns[i]` is the number of columns in the `i-th` table.

You should be able to perform the following operations:

*   Insert a row in a specific table. Each row you insert has an id. The id is assigned using an auto-increment strategy where the id of the first row is 1, the id of the second row is 2, etc.
*   Select a cell from any table with a specific `rowId` and `columnId`.

Implement the `SQL` class:

*   `SQL(List<String> names, List<Integer> columns)` Initializes the `SQL` object.
*   `void insertRow(String name, List<String> row)` Inserts a row into the table `name`. It is guaranteed that the table exists and the size of `row` equals the number of columns in the table.
*   `String selectCell(String name, int rowId, int columnId)` Returns the value in the cell in the row `rowId` and column `columnId` from the table `name`.

## Example 1:

**Input:**
["SQL", "insertRow", "selectCell", "insertRow", "selectCell", "selectCell"]
[[["one", "two", "three"], [2, 3, 1]], ["two", ["first", "second", "third"]], ["two", 1, 3], ["two", ["fourth", "fifth", "sixth"]], ["two", 1, 2], ["two", 2, 1]]
**Output:**
[null, null, "third", null, "second", "fourth"]
**Explanation:**
SQL sql = new SQL(["one", "two", "three"], [2, 3, 1]);
sql.insertRow("two", ["first", "second", "third"]); // Adds a row to the table "two". Its id is 1.
sql.selectCell("two", 1, 3); // return "third", finds the value of the third column in the row with id 1 of the table "two".
sql.insertRow("two", ["fourth", "fifth", "sixth"]); // Adds another row to the table "two". Its id is 2.
sql.selectCell("two", 1, 2); // return "second", finds the value of the second column in the row with id 1 of the table "two".
sql.selectCell("two", 2, 1); // return "fourth", finds the value of the first column in the row with id 2 of the table "two".

## Constraints:

*   `n == names.length == columns.length`
*   `1 <= n <= 10^4`
*   `1 <= names[i].length, row[i].length, name.length <= 10`
*   `names[i]`, `row[i]`, and `name` consist of lowercase English letters.
*   `1 <= columns[i] <= 10`
*   All the strings of `names` are unique.
*   `insertRow` will be called at most `2000` times.
*   `selectCell` will be called at most `2000` times.

solutions.name: HashMap of Tables
solutions.description: Map table names to a list of rows. Each row is a List<String>. insertRow appends to the list. selectCell indexes by rowId-1 and columnId-1.

solutions.name: HashMap with Row ID Tracking
solutions.description: Use a nested HashMap: table name maps to a map of rowId to row data. Track auto-increment ID per table. SelectCell looks up by table name, rowId, and columnId.
